newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican asks English bishops to delay visit.
newsitem.headline: Vatican asks English bishops to delay visit.

text.p: The Vatican has asked English and Welsh bishops to postpone a visit scheduled for this month, apparently to give Pope John Paul time to rest after a trip to the Czech Republic, Church sources said on Wednesday.

The Roman Catholic bishops had been due to make the three-day visit from April 28 to 30. The 76-year-old Pope is due to visit the Czech Republic from April 25 to 27 and would have returned on the eve of the scheduled meetings.
The sources said the Vatican requested the delay apparently to make sure the Pope would have time to rest if he needed to after returning from the weekend in Prague and the town of Kradec Kralove.
No new dates for the meetings have been set but they would most likely take place in the summer, the sources said.
Group visits to the Vatican by national bishops' conferences are made every five years.
During the visits, the Pope meets individually with each bishop and addresses the group. The bishops also meet with heads of various Vatican departments.
The Pope, who turns 77 next month, has had a series of health problems over the past few years.
But he appeared rested and in relatively good form at his weekly general audience on Wednesday, his first since last weekend's trip to Sarajevo.
